qp_dispositions.rationale: Direct recognition of whether entries are real is definition-level classification; no distinct multi-step JEE reasoning mechanism is present in the source possibility.

A parameterized matrix can require simultaneous constraints from multiple entries; extracting and solving all reality conditions is a reusable parameter-constraint mechanism. Candidate only; academic approval and question-level validation remain pending.
For real matrices, entrywise addition and subtraction preserve real entries directly. This is a basic closure fact and does not justify a separate archetype from the stated possibility.

Products and integer powers of real matrices remain real by entrywise closure under multiplication and addition. The stated possibility is a direct closure check without a distinct reasoning mechanism.

Determining when a linear combination of real matrices remains real can require constraints on complex scalar coefficients and matrix linear independence; this differs from imposing reality conditions on matrix entries themselves. Candidate only; validate against representative JEE questions before approval.
Transpose only reorders the entries of a real matrix, so realness is preserved directly. This is a definition-level closure property rather than a distinct JEE archetype.

For a real matrix, entrywise conjugation leaves every entry unchanged and the conjugate transpose reduces to the transpose. The stated possibility is direct property recognition without an independent inference mechanism.

The inverse of an invertible real matrix is real, as follows from standard inverse/determinant or linear-system properties. The source possibility states a direct closure theorem and does not by itself define a distinct JEE archetype.

Polynomial and defined rational expressions with real coefficients preserve real entries under the stated operations. This is a direct closure/property check; a richer task would require a separately specified mechanism.
Trace, determinant, minors and cofactors of a real matrix are real by their definitions as sums and products of real entries. This is direct property application, not a distinct archetype.

The inclusion chain for integer-, rational-, real- and complex-entry matrices follows entrywise from the corresponding scalar number sets. This is direct hierarchy recognition and does not justify a separate JEE archetype.

An m×n real matrix has mn independently selectable real entries by definition. Counting these parameters is a direct dimension/counting fact; a distinct linear-algebra constraint problem would need a separately specified source possibility.
Translating R^{m×n} or M_{m×n}(R) is notation recognition for the set of real matrices of fixed order. It is prerequisite knowledge rather than a distinct assessment mechanism.
Classifying a matrix as real or complex from its entries is direct definition-level recognition. It is retained as foundation content and is not a separate JEE archetype.
Taking the complex conjugate entrywise is a direct operation. Without additional constraints or a multi-step inference, the source possibility does not justify a distinct JEE archetype.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine parameter conditions under which a parametric matrix is a real matrix
archetypes.archetype: Simultaneous reality constraints in a parameterized matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Translate the requirement that an entire parameterized matrix is real into simultaneous zero-imaginary-part constraints on its entries, then solve the resulting parameter system.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Inspect each matrix entry; isolate its imaginary part; set every imaginary part to zero; solve the simultaneous equations; check that the resulting parameter values satisfy every entry.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine whether scalar multiplication or linear combinations yield a real matrix and identify conditions on scalar coefficients
archetypes.archetype: Reality of a linear combination of real matrices
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Determine the scalar-coefficient conditions under which a linear combination of real matrices has only real entries, using entrywise imaginary-part equations and any stated linear-independence information.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Write the imaginary parts of the scalar coefficients; form the matrix equation for the imaginary component of the combination; use the matrix independence or dependence conditions to solve for admissible coefficients; verify the result entrywise.
variation_dimensions: number of matrices in the combination
presence of zero or repeated matrices
